records.title: Communication Disorders in a Social World: Barriers and Bridges
records.header: SPHSC 110 Communication Disorders in a Social World: Barriers and Bridges (3) SSc
records.text: SPHSC 110 Communication Disorders in a Social World: Barriers and Bridges (3) SSc Examines societal and media perspectives of communication processes and individuals with communication challenges. Applies disability and ableism frameworks to examine historical and contemporary factors that can enhance or create barriers to communication across contexts. Explores the roles of communication professionals and emphasizes advocacy, inclusive practices, and respect for communicative diversity. Offered: AWSp.

records.title: Contextualizing Disability and Communication in Speech, Language, and Hearing Sciences
records.header: SPHSC 200 Contextualizing Disability and Communication in Speech, Language, and Hearing Sciences (3) DIV
records.text: SPHSC 200 Contextualizing Disability and Communication in Speech, Language, and Hearing Sciences (3) DIV Explores how communication and disability are shaped by identity, power, and society. Examines topics such as disparities in health and education, ableism, neurodiversity, and intersectionality, with an emphasis on the lived experiences of those with communication disorders. Addresses implications for research and practice in speech, language, and hearing sciences. Offered: W.

records.title: Introduction to Speech and Hearing Sciences
records.header: SPHSC 250 Introduction to Speech and Hearing Sciences (3) SSc/NSc
records.text: SPHSC 250 Introduction to Speech and Hearing Sciences (3) SSc/NSc Introduction to the field of speech and hearing sciences and its associated professions. Provides broad overview of normal and impaired speech, language, swallowing, hearing, and balance disorders, and clinical practice settings. Discusses impact of social-cultural, ethical, and technological factors in diagnosis, treatment, and research. Required for majors; open to nonmajors. Offered: AS.

records.title: The Nature of Sound
records.header: SPHSC 261 The Nature of Sound (3) NSc
records.text: SPHSC 261 The Nature of Sound (3) NSc Fundamental principles of sound and vibration with emphasis on examples relevant to the speech and hearing systems. Required for majors; open to nonmajors. Course overlaps with: SPHSC 354 and SPHSC 355. Offered: A.

records.title: Phonetics: Theory and Transcription
records.header: SPHSC 302 Phonetics: Theory and Transcription (4) A&H
records.text: SPHSC 302 Phonetics: Theory and Transcription (4) A&H Introduction to phonetics for speech and hearing sciences. Topics include broad and narrow transcription of spoken English using the International Phonetic Alphabet, articulatory classification of the consonants and vowels of English, non-native accented speech, dialectal variations, developmental speech patterns, speech disorders, and clinical applications of phonetics in speech and hearing sciences. Course overlaps with: SPHSC 355. Prerequisite: LING 200. Offered: W.

records.title: Language Science
records.header: SPHSC 303 Language Science (3) A&H
records.text: SPHSC 303 Language Science (3) A&H Introduction to techniques of linguistic analysis (morphology, syntax, semantics, pragmatics, etc.) used in clinical application to understand communication capacities in individuals. Course overlaps with: SPHSC 352. Prerequisite: LING 200 or LING 400. Offered: SpS.

records.title: Speech and Language Acquisition
records.header: SPHSC 304 Speech and Language Acquisition (5) SSc
records.text: SPHSC 304 Speech and Language Acquisition (5) SSc Introduction to the study of speech and language from a developmental perspective. Overview of typical communicative development patterns and milestones in English speaking children. Application to broader issues in communication science and development. Course overlaps with: SPHSC 352. Offered: A.

records.title: Developmental Communication and Swallowing Disorders
records.header: SPHSC 305 Developmental Communication and Swallowing Disorders (3) NSc
records.text: SPHSC 305 Developmental Communication and Swallowing Disorders (3) NSc Etiology and nature of developmental communication and swallowing disorders. Behavioral characteristics and common treatment approaches for language delay and disorders, developmental apraxia of speech, phonological disorders, fluency, craniofacial anomalies, cognitive-communication disorders, and feeding/swallowing disorders. Required for majors; open to nonmajors. Course overlaps with: SPHSC 427. Prerequisite: SPHSC 250; SPHSC 304; and SPHSC 320. Offered: W.
records.schedulingNote: Catalog prerequisites/offering patterns are not current registration permission or guaranteed future offerings.

records.title: Acquired Communication and Swallowing Disorders
records.header: SPHSC 306 Acquired Communication and Swallowing Disorders (3) NSc
records.text: SPHSC 306 Acquired Communication and Swallowing Disorders (3) NSc Etiology and nature of acquired speech, language, cognitive-communication and swallowing disorders in adult and geriatric populations. Behavioral characteristics and common treatment approaches related to neurological and other conditions such as stroke, traumatic brain injury, dementia, degenerative diseases, and head and neck cancer. Course overlaps with: SPHSC 429. Prerequisite: SPHSC 250 and SPHSC 320. Offered: W.

records.title: Preparation for Careers and Graduate Study in Speech and Hearing Sciences
records.header: SPHSC 316 Preparation for Careers and Graduate Study in Speech and Hearing Sciences (2)
records.text: SPHSC 316 Preparation for Careers and Graduate Study in Speech and Hearing Sciences (2) Post-bachelor employment options. Emphasis on clinical and research career paths. Strategies for pursuing graduate study in speech-language pathology and audiology. Opportunities for individual reflective work, peer review, professional portfolio development, and planning. Credit/no-credit only. Offered: SpS.

records.title: Anatomy and Physiology of Speech and Swallowing
records.header: SPHSC 320 Anatomy and Physiology of Speech and Swallowing (5) NSc
records.text: SPHSC 320 Anatomy and Physiology of Speech and Swallowing (5) NSc Anatomy and physiology of the speech and swallowing mechanism, including the respiratory, phonatory, and resonatory systems and their neural control. Examples and laboratory work are directed toward clinical issues in speech-language pathology. Course overlaps with: SPHSC 353. Offered: A.

records.title: Development of Speech and Language
records.header: SPHSC 352 Development of Speech and Language (4)
records.text: SPHSC 352 Development of Speech and Language (4) Examines typical patterns and processes of child speech and language development and the methods by which they are documented and analyzed. Explores basic communication development from birth to age five in terms of form, content, and use, and establishes connections between speech and language acquisition and other human developmental domains. Course overlaps with: SPHSC 303 and SPHSC 304. Offered: S.
records.schedulingNote: Catalog prerequisites/offering patterns are not current registration permission or guaranteed future offerings.

records.title: Anatomy, Physiology, and Science of Speech and Swallowing
records.header: SPHSC 353 Anatomy, Physiology, and Science of Speech and Swallowing (4)
records.text: SPHSC 353 Anatomy, Physiology, and Science of Speech and Swallowing (4) Examines the anatomy, physiology, and scientific principles underlying human speech production and swallowing processes. Explores the systems of respiration, phonation, resonance, articulation, mastication, and swallowing, connecting these integrated functions and associated scientific theories to current clinical practice in the field. Course overlaps with: SPHSC 320. Offered: S.

records.title: Anatomy, Physiology, and Science of Hearing
records.header: SPHSC 354 Anatomy, Physiology, and Science of Hearing (4)
records.text: SPHSC 354 Anatomy, Physiology, and Science of Hearing (4) Examines the anatomy, physiology, and scientific principles underlying human hearing and sound perception processes. Explores the auditory system, limitations of human audition, and methods by which hearing can be measured and analyzed. Course overlaps with: SPHSC 261 and SPHSC 461. Offered: A.

records.title: Phonetics and Speech Acoustics
records.header: SPHSC 355 Phonetics and Speech Acoustics (4)
records.text: SPHSC 355 Phonetics and Speech Acoustics (4) Examines articulatory and acoustic features of American English phonemes and their relevance to speech-language pathology clinical practice. Explains broad and narrow transcription methods used by clinicians to document and analyze spoken language in all its variations. Course overlaps with: SPHSC 261 and SPHSC 302. Offered: A.

records.title: Hearing Disorders
records.header: SPHSC 371 Hearing Disorders (4) SSc/NSc
records.text: SPHSC 371 Hearing Disorders (4) SSc/NSc Introduction to abnormal hearing and pathologies of the ear. Audiometric assessment and correlates of hearing function, including standard pure-tone audiometry, speech audiometry, and basic impedance audiometry. Communicative and social consequences of hearing loss. Overview of management and treatment of children and adults. Required for majors; open to nonmajors. Course overlaps with: SPHSC 428. Prerequisite: SPHSC 250. Offered: WS.

records.header: SPHSC 405 Clinical Decision Making in Speech-Language Pathology (4) NSc
records.text: SPHSC 405 Clinical Decision Making in Speech-Language Pathology (4) NSc Introduction to principles and practices of assessment and treatment for speech-language pathologists. Includes foundation in skills and issues common in assessment and treatment across communication and swallowing disorders. Prerequisite: SPHSC 250; SPHSC 305; and SPHSC 306 Offered: Sp.

records.title: Speech, Language, Hearing, and the Brain
records.header: SPHSC 425 Speech, Language, Hearing, and the Brain (5) SSc/NSc
records.text: SPHSC 425 Speech, Language, Hearing, and the Brain (5) SSc/NSc Addresses the neural bases of topics in speech, language, and hearing with an emphasis on the normal aspects of central nervous system anatomy, physiology, and function. Gives attention to issues relevant to understanding disordered systems and to points of contemporary debate among neuroscientists. Course overlaps with: SPHSC 426. Prerequisite: SPHSC 250. Offered: Sp.

records.title: Neurological Foundations of Communication and Swallowing
records.header: SPHSC 426 Neurological Foundations of Communication and Swallowing (4)
records.text: SPHSC 426 Neurological Foundations of Communication and Swallowing (4) Examines the human nervous system's role in the processes of speech, language, hearing, cognition, and swallowing. Emphasizes key scientific principles underlying these processes as well as typical aspects of central and peripheral nervous system anatomy, physiology, and function. Course overlaps with: SPHSC 425. Offered: W.

records.title: Pediatric Communication and Swallowing Disorders
records.header: SPHSC 427 Pediatric Communication and Swallowing Disorders (4)
records.text: SPHSC 427 Pediatric Communication and Swallowing Disorders (4) Explores pediatric communication and swallowing disorders, emphasizing primary etiologies, behavioral characteristics, as well as developmental and psychosocial effects. Examines common clinical approaches and tools for diagnosis and treatment, incorporating relevant pediatric professional practice issues related to research evidence, ethics, equity, cultural and linguistic responsiveness, and interprofessional collaboration. Course overlaps with: SPHSC 305 and SPHSC 406. Offered: W.

records.header: SPHSC 428 Audiology and Hearing Disorders (4)
records.text: SPHSC 428 Audiology and Hearing Disorders (4) Explores disorders of the human auditory system across the lifespan, emphasizing primary etiologies, behavioral characteristics, as well as psychosocial and health effects. Examines common clinical approaches and tools used for diagnosis and treatment, incorporating relevant professional practice issues related to research evidence, ethics, equity, cultural and linguistic responsiveness, and interprofessional collaboration. Course overlaps with: SPHSC 371 and SPHSC 481. Offered: Sp.

records.text: SPHSC 429 Adult Communication and Swallowing Disorders (4) Explores adult and geriatric communication and swallowing disorders, emphasizing primary etiologies, behavioral characteristics, recovery trajectories, as well as psychosocial and health effects. records.title: Hearing Science
records.header: SPHSC 461 Hearing Science (5) NSc
records.text: SPHSC 461 Hearing Science (5) NSc Explores basic structures and functions related to the ear, the auditory nervous system, and hearing. Examines how the human auditory system constructs and interprets sounds and the influence of attention and memory on hearing. Addresses impacts of auditory system damage on hearing and overall functioning. Course overlaps with: SPHSC 354. Prerequisite: SPHSC 261. Offered: Sp.
